(a) Secure Payments for States and Counties Containing Federal Land.—
        (1) Secure payments.—Section 101 of the Secure Rural Schools and Community Self-Determination Act of 2000 (16 U.S.C. 7111) is amended, in subsections (a) and (b), by striking “and 2018” each place it appears and inserting “2018, 2019, and 2020”. 
        (2) Payments to states and counties.—
            (A) Election to receive payment amount.—Section 102(b) of the Secure Rural Schools and Community Self-Determination Act of 2000 (16 U.S.C. 7112(b)) is amended—
                (i) in paragraph (1)(D)—
                    (I) in the subparagraph heading, by striking “for fiscal years 2017 and 2018” and inserting “for each of fiscal years 2017 through 2020”; and 
                    (II) by striking “for fiscal years 2017 or 2018” and inserting “for each of fiscal years 2017 through 2020”; and  
                (ii) in paragraph (2), in subparagraphs (A) and (B), by striking “for fiscal years 2017 and 2018” each place it appears and inserting “for each of fiscal years 2017 through 2020”.  
            (B) Expenditure rules for eligible counties.—Section 102(d) of the Secure Rural Schools and Community Self-Determination Act of 2000 (16 U.S.C. 7112(d)) is amended—
                (i) in paragraph (1)(F)—
                    (I) in the subparagraph heading, by striking “for fiscal years 2017 and 2018” and inserting “for each of fiscal years 2017 through 2020”; and 
                    (II) by striking “for fiscal years 2017 and 2018” and inserting “for each of fiscal years 2017 through 2020”; and  
                (ii) in paragraph (3)(D)—
                    (I) in the subparagraph heading, by striking “for fiscal years 2017 and 2018” and inserting “for each of fiscal years 2017 through 2020”; and 
                    (II) by striking “for fiscal years 2017 and 2018” and inserting “for each of fiscal years 2017 through 2020”.   
            (C) Distribution of payments to eligible counties.—Section 103(d)(2) of the Secure Rural Schools and Community Self-Determination Act of 2000 (16 U.S.C. 7113(d)(2)) is amended by striking “through and for fiscal 
years 2017 and 2018” and inserting “through 2015 and for each of fiscal years 2017 through 2020”.   
    (b) Extension of Authority To Conduct Special Projects on Federal Land.—
        (1) Existing advisory committees.—Section 205(a)(4) of the Secure Rural Schools and Community Self-Determination Act of 2000 (16 U.S.C. 7125(a)(4)) is amended by striking “September 29, 2018” each place it appears and inserting “December 20, 2021”. 
        (2) Termination of authority.—Section 208 of the Secure Rural Schools and Community Self-Determination Act of 2000 (16 U.S.C. 7128) is amended—
            (A) in subsection (a), by striking “2020” and inserting “2022”; and 
            (B) in subsection (b), by striking “2021” and inserting “2023”.   
    (c) Extension of Authority To Expend County Funds.—Section 304 of the Secure Rural Schools and Community Self-Determination Act of 2000 (16 U.S.C. 7144) is amended—
        (1) in subsection (a), by striking “2020” and inserting “2022”; and 
        (2) in subsection (b), by striking “2021” and inserting “2023”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that this section only changes dates and extends payments to states and counties, which is funding rather than participation. But subsection (b) extends the life of the existing advisory committees under the Secure Rural Schools Act and the authority for special projects on federal land. Those committees are understood, from background knowledge rather than this text, to be made up of local non-federal members who recommend projects to the Secretary. Extending them continues outside involvement in federal decisions, though the call is close because the section sets out no new process of its own.
fable.s: Existing advisory committees.—Section 205(a)(4) of the Secure Rural Schools and Community Self-Determination Act of 2000 (16 U.S.C. 7125(a)(4)) is amended by striking “September 29, 2018” each place it appears and inserting “December 20, 2021”

It merely extends the statutory authority for mechanisms defined elsewhere. The definition requires the section to involve consultation or coordination with outsiders; extending a deadline for an existing, undefined committee does not constitute a new requirement for participation in this specific text.

qwen_block.b:
1.  **Think briefly**: The section primarily consists of technical amendments extending the expiration dates of various provisions in the Secure Rural Schools and Community Self-Determination Act of 2000. It extends payment periods, expenditure rules, and the authority to conduct special projects. Subsection (b)(1) mentions "Existing advisory committees" and extends their authority until December 20, 2021. However, the text itself does not establish a new advisory committee, nor does it describe the composition of the existing ones (i.e., whether they include non-federal members). It merely extends the statutory authority for committees that are presumably already established elsewhere. The definition of participation requires that the section *involve* consultation or coordination with outsiders. Merely extending the deadline for an existing mechanism without describing the participatory nature of that mechanism in the current text is generally considered "No" because the text itself does not mandate or describe the participation process; it just keeps the legal authority alive. Furthermore, the bulk of the text is about payments and expenditure rules, which are administrative/financial provisions. The mention of "advisory committees" is a reference to an existing structure, not a creation or description of a participatory process in this specific section. Therefore, the section does not itself recommend or require participation in the sense of defining a process involving outsiders.

opus.w: Section 205 of the Secure Rural Schools Act sets up Resource Advisory Committees. Their members are local, non-federal stakeholders (industry, environmental groups, local officials, the public) who recommend special projects on federal land to the Secretary. This section extends those committees, which keeps outsiders involved in federal decisions. The changes to payment dates are about benefits and would not count on their own, but the advisory-committee extension crosses the federal boundary.

Tempting reading: most of this section only changes fiscal-year dates for payments to states and counties. Payments are benefits, so they do not count as participation.

Why that fails: subsection (b)(1) also extends "existing advisory committees" under Section 205 of the Secure Rural Schools Act. These are the Resource Advisory Committees. By law, their members are local, non-federal stakeholders who recommend special projects on federal land to the Secretary. Extending their terms keeps outsiders involved in federal decisions.

qwen_chat.s: Section 101 of the Secure Rural Schools and Community Self-Determination Act of 2000 (16 U.S.C. 7111) is amended, in subsections (a) and (b), by striking “and 2018” each place it appears and inserting “2018, 2019, and 2020”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: The section mentions "Existing advisory committees" in subsection (b)(1), which might suggest participation. However, the text only extends the expiration date of these committees; it does not establish new participation mechanisms or describe the composition of the committees in a way that confirms outside involvement in this specific section. More importantly, the bulk of the section deals with extending funding authorization dates and expenditure rules for states and counties. Extending the duration of a grant or payment program is not participation. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants. While states are outside entities, receiving funds or having the authority to spend them is not "consultation or coordination... before making a decision" by the federal government in the participatory sense defined (e.g., advisory boards, comment periods). The extension of the advisory committee's existence is a procedural extension of an existing body, but the primary action here is fiscal extension. Even if the advisory committees involve outsiders, this specific text merely extends their statutory authority date, which is a legislative housekeeping measure rather than a direct mandate for participation in a specific decision-making process within this section. However, looking closer at the definition: "Participation is when the federal government may or must consult or coordinate with people outside of the government before making a decision." Does extending the life of an advisory committee constitute participation? The committee itself is the mechanism. But the section doesn't *require* consultation in this text; it just says the committee's authority lasts longer. The core of the section is about money (payments, expenditures). The definition says "It does not include applications for benefits or grants." This section extends the availability of funds. It does not describe a process where the federal government consults with outsiders *in this section*. The mention of advisory committees is incidental to the date extension. Therefore, the label is No.
